references.text: God reveals his name YHWH to Moses in response to the question in verse 13, confirming that he is the God of the fathers—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God explains that he revealed himself to the patriarchs as El Shaddai, but by the name YHWH he was not known to them, which deepens the meaning of this revelation of his name.
Jacob also asks for God's name at Peniel, showing that the question of God's name was important in the time of the patriarchs.
Manoah asks the angel of the Lord for his name and is told that it is wonderful, illustrating the mystery connected to God's name.
God reveals himself to Abram as El Shaddai (God Almighty), an earlier revelation of God's name to the patriarchs.
Moses expresses concern that the Israelites will not believe him, which relates to his question about God's name in 3:13.
Jesus uses the expression 'ἐγὼ εἰμί' (I am), linking it to God's self-revelation in Exodus 3:14 where God says, 'I am who I am.'
Those who know God's name trust in him—the meaning of the name for trust and relationship with God.
The question 'what is his name?' is asked about God and his Son, reflecting Moses' question about God's name.
